newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bulk carrier crew rescued in Indian Ocean.
newsitem.headline: Bulk carrier crew rescued in Indian Ocean.

text.p: All 21 crew members of a Panamanian-flagged bulk carrier sinking in the Indian Ocean were picked up by a British tanker on Friday about four hours after abandoning ship, Australian search and rescue officials said.

The crew of the 150,000 deadweight tonne Goodwill took to the lifeboats after the vessel struck a seamount -- a volcano under the water -- and began to take in water, a spokesman for the Australian Maritime Rescue Co-Ordination Centre said.

The spokesman said crew members were picked up by the British tanker British Skill and would be taken to Cocos Islands, an Australian territory about 900 miles off Western Australia. "All 21 are safe and well," the spokesman said.
The Korean-owned ship hit the rocks about 60 miles southwest of Cocos Islands while on a trip from Dampier, Western Australia, to the Suez Canal with a cargo of iron ore.
A salvage operation was being organised in Singapore and a tug already in the region was on its way to the stricken vessel, the search and rescue spokesman said.
"It's still floating but slowly sinking," he said.
The ship's Korean officers and Indonesian crew would be repatriated from the Cocos Islands, he said.
